newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria Shell turns to locals to secure pipelines.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria Shell turns to locals to secure pipelines.

text.p: The local unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group said on Friday it would embark on recruitmant from local communities to man its facilities in response to rising sabotage of its pipelines.

"We are floating a security outfit that will be constituted by indigenes of the communities to carry out all round checks on our facilities," said a spokesman of Shell Petroleum Development Company Nigeria (SPDC).
"It is the only practical thing we can do now to check the growing sabotage of our facilities," the spokesman added.
SPDC is a joint venture between Royal Dutch Shell Group and state-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC).
The company has come under attacks by host communities in the restive oil-producing Niger Delta of Nigeria resulting in oil spillages through burst pipelines.

The spokesman said 95 percent of the spills were due to sabotage. "By employing the indigenes as security guards, we are sending a message that it is in the best interest of the communities that oil production is unhindered," he added.

The current edition of the in-house Shell newsletter said a total of 35,000 barrels of oil was spilled in the first three months of this year and another 12,000 barrels spilled in the months of April and May.
Shell refuses to pay compensation for spillages ascertained to have been caused deliberately by local communities for the purpose of receiving money from the multinational oil company.
